title: Your Business Insurance Never Priced AI. Now It’s Writing It Out
ai_summary: Insurers are adding AI exclusions to standard policies, leaving AI liability on deployers. Specialist policies like Armilla's $25 million limit and Lloyd's-backed products are emerging, while a federal backstop is proposed. Market projections for AI insurance premiums range from $4.77 billion to $500 billion by 2030.

title: Does AI need its own insurance market? Brokers are already finding out
ai_summary: Brokers are increasingly asked whether AI needs its own insurance market, with a poll showing half expect AI-specific insurance to become a major line. Standalone AI policies like Armilla AI's US$25 million cover and Munich Re's aiSure are emerging, while others add AI liability to existing policies. Brokers face ambiguity from silent AI coverage in cyber and technology policies.

title: Five worthy reads: The next big insurance market no one is talking about yet
ai_summary: AI hallucination insurance is emerging as a market, with Armilla launching a policy covering legal claims from AI errors. AI-related lawsuits in the US grew 978% between 2021 and 2025, and the Florida Supreme Court set new rules for AI-assisted filings. The article argues conventional insurance fails to cover these risks.
